name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q01 - Classification of solids and semiconductors

questiontext.text:
Match Column I with Column II:

Column I Column II
A. Metals (Conductors) I. Forbidden energy band gap \(E_g > 3\text{ eV}\) (e.g., Diamond with \(5.4\text{ eV}\))
B. Elemental Semiconductors II. Conduction band overlaps valence band or band gap is zero (\(E_g \approx 0\))
C. Insulators III. Compound semiconductors such as CdS and GaAs
D. Inorganic Compound Semiconductors IV. Silicon (Si) and Germanium (Ge) with narrow band gaps (\(0.2\text{ eV} < E_g < 3\text{ eV}\))

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
Solids are classified into metals, semiconductors, and insulators based on their energy band structures, forbidden energy gaps (\(E_g\)), and elemental or compound chemical composition.

Step-by-Step Item Matching:
Evaluating each item in Column I with its appropriate description in Column II:
• Metals (Conductors): Characterized by an overlapping conduction and valence band where \(E_g \approx 0\), allowing free movement of valence electrons. Thus, item A matches description II.
• Elemental Semiconductors: Composed of pure Group 14 elements Si and Ge having small, finite band gaps (\(E_g \approx 1.1\text{ eV}\) for Si and \(E_g \approx 0.7\text{ eV}\) for Ge). Thus, item B matches description IV.
• Insulators: Possess a very wide forbidden energy gap (\(E_g > 3\text{ eV}\), e.g., diamond with \(E_g \approx 5.4\text{ eV}\)) that prevents thermal promotion of electrons into the conduction band at ordinary temperatures. Thus, item C matches description I.
• Inorganic Compound Semiconductors: Formed by combinations of inorganic elements such as cadmium sulphide (CdS) and gallium arsenide (GaAs). Thus, item D matches description III.

Check and Final Answer:
Combining the individual pairings yields the overall mapping: A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q02 - Doping impurities and extrinsic semiconductor properties

questiontext.text:
Match Column I with Column II:

Column I Column II
A. Pentavalent dopant (Donor impurity) I. Introduces an acceptor energy level \(E_A\) slightly above the valence band
B. Trivalent dopant (Acceptor impurity) II. Introduces a donor energy level \(E_D\) slightly below the conduction band
C. \(n\)-type semiconductor III. Mobile holes are majority carriers (\(n_h \gg n_e\)) with bulk crystal charge neutrality
D. \(p\)-type semiconductor IV. Conduction electrons are majority carriers (\(n_e \gg n_h\)) with bulk crystal charge neutrality

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
Extrinsic semiconductors are created by adding specific trivalent or pentavalent impurity dopants to pure tetravalent crystals, which creates localized impurity energy levels and alters majority and minority carrier populations while conserving electrical neutrality.

Step-by-Step Item Matching:
Evaluating each item in Column I with its appropriate description in Column II:
• Pentavalent dopant (Donor impurity): Elements like phosphorus, arsenic, or antimony provide extra electrons bound by small ionization energies (\(\sim 0.01\text{ to } 0.05\text{ eV}\)), creating donor energy states \(E_D\) located just below the conduction band edge \(E_C\). Thus, item A matches description II.
• Trivalent dopant (Acceptor impurity): Elements like boron, aluminum, or indium create vacancies (holes) that easily capture valence electrons, creating acceptor energy states \(E_A\) located just above the valence band edge \(E_V\). Thus, item B matches description I.
• \(n\)-type semiconductor: Pentavalent doping causes electrons to vastly outnumber holes (\(n_e \gg n_h\)), yet the positive donor ions exactly balance excess electron charges, keeping the bulk crystal electrically neutral. Thus, item C matches description IV.
• \(p\)-type semiconductor: Trivalent doping causes holes to vastly outnumber electrons (\(n_h \gg n_e\)), yet the negative acceptor ions balance the mobile holes, preserving overall electrical neutrality. Thus, item D matches description III.

Check and Final Answer:
Combining the individual pairings yields the overall mapping: A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q03 - Operating states and characteristics of semiconductor devices

questiontext.text:
Match Column I with Column II:

Column I Column II
A. Unbiased \(p\text{-}n\) junction at equilibrium I. Barrier height rises to \((V_0 + V)\), widening depletion layer with tiny minority carrier drift current
B. Forward biased \(p\text{-}n\) junction II. Barrier height falls to \((V_0 - V)\), narrowing depletion layer with heavy minority carrier injection in mA
C. Reverse biased \(p\text{-}n\) junction III. Forward diffusion current exactly balances reverse drift current, producing zero net current
D. Full-wave rectifier with capacitor filter IV. Converts both half-cycles into unidirectional pulses whose discharge rate across \(R_L\) is governed by time constant \(C R_L\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
The electrical response of a \(p\text{-}n\) junction depends directly on the polarity of the applied bias, which modulates the built-in barrier potential, changes the depletion layer width, and alters carrier transport, while filtering smoothing circuits rely on capacitive time constants.

Step-by-Step Item Matching:
Evaluating each item in Column I with its appropriate description in Column II:
• Unbiased \(p\text{-}n\) junction at equilibrium: At equilibrium without bias, the forward diffusion of majority carriers across the concentration gradient is dynamically and exactly cancelled by the drift of minority carriers under the built-in electric field, resulting in strictly zero net current across the junction. Thus, item A matches description III.
• Forward biased \(p\text{-}n\) junction: When the \(p\)-side is connected to the positive terminal and \(n\)-side to the negative terminal, the applied voltage opposes the built-in barrier potential, reducing the barrier to \((V_0 - V)\) and narrowing the depletion region. This enables significant minority carrier injection that yields a forward diffusion current measured in milliamperes. Thus, item B matches description II.
• Reverse biased \(p\text{-}n\) junction: When the \(n\)-side is made positive and \(p\)-side negative, the external voltage aids the built-in field, raising the potential barrier to \((V_0 + V)\) and widening the depletion layer. Majority diffusion is suppressed, leaving only a minute drift current (saturation current) of thermally generated minority carriers measured in microamperes. Thus, item C matches description I.
• Full-wave rectifier with capacitor filter: In a full-wave rectifier, both positive and negative input half-cycles conduct through alternate diodes in the identical direction across the load resistor. The parallel capacitor charges to peak voltage during conduction and discharges through the load resistor with an exponential decay rate dictated by time constant \(\tau = C R_L\). Thus, item D matches description IV.

Check and Final Answer:
Combining the individual pairings yields the overall mapping: A-III, B-II, C-I, D-IV.
